public_domain_references.web: They have set up kings, but not by me. They have made princes, and I didn’t approve. Of their silver and their gold they have made themselves idols, that they may be cut off.
public_domain_references.asv: They have set up kings, but not by me; they have made princes, and I knew it not: of their silver and their gold have they made them idols, that they may be cut off.
public_domain_references.kjv: They have set up kings, but not by me: they have made princes, and I knew [it] not: of their silver and their gold have they made them idols, that they may be cut off.
public_domain_references.brenton: They have made kings for themselves, but not by me: they have ruled, but they did not make it known to me: [of] their silver and their gold they have made images to themselves, that they might be destroyed.

pob.text: He has rejected your calf[a], O Samaria; my anger burns against them[b]. How long will they be incapable of innocence?

spob.text: He has rejected your calf,[a] Samaria. My anger burns against them. How long will they remain unable to be innocent?[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: He has rejected your calf, O Samaria. My anger burns against them. How long will they be incapable of innocence?
public_domain_references.web: Let Samaria throw out his calf idol! My anger burns against them! How long will it be until they are capable of purity?
public_domain_references.asv: He hath cast off thy calf, O Samaria; mine anger is kindled against them: how long will it be ere they attain to innocency?
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ Thy calf, O Samaria, hath cast [thee] off; mine anger is kindled against them: how long [will it be] ere they attain to innocency?
public_domain_references.brenton: Cast off thy calf, O Samaria; mine anger is kindled against them: how long will they be unable to purge themselves in Israel?

pob.text: For it is from Israel[a]; a craftsman made it, and it is not God. Indeed[b], the calf of Samaria will become splinters.

spob.text: For this calf-idol came from Israel. A craftsman made it, and it is not God. Samaria’s calf-idol will certainly be broken into splinters.

public_domain_references.bsb: For this thing is from Israel— a craftsman made it, and it is not God. It will be broken to pieces, that calf of Samaria.
public_domain_references.web: For this is even from Israel! The workman made it, and it is no God; indeed, the calf of Samaria shall be broken in pieces.
public_domain_references.asv: For from Israel is even this; the workman made it, and it is no God; yea, the calf of Samaria shall be broken in pieces.
public_domain_references.kjv: For from Israel [was] it also: the workman made it; therefore it [is] not God: but the calf of Samaria shall be broken in pieces.
public_domain_references.brenton: Whereas the workman made it, and it is not God; wherefore thy calf, Samaria, was a deceiver:

pob.text: For they sow the wind[a], and they will reap the whirlwind. The standing grain has no head; it will yield no flour. Even if it should yield[c][b], strangers will swallow it up.

spob.text: For they sow the wind, and they will harvest a whirlwind. Their grain has no heads and will produce no flour. Even if it yields something,[a] foreigners will swallow it up.

public_domain_references.bsb: For they sow the wind, and they shall reap the whirlwind. There is no standing grain; what sprouts fails to yield flour. Even if it should produce, the foreigners would swallow it up.
public_domain_references.web: For they sow the wind, and they will reap the whirlwind. He has no standing grain. The stalk will yield no head. If it does yield, strangers will swallow it up.
public_domain_references.asv: For they sow the wind, and they shall reap the whirlwind: he hath no standing grain; the blade shall yield no meal; if so be it yield, strangers shall swallow it up.
public_domain_references.kjv: For they have sown the wind, and they shall reap the whirlwind: it hath no stalk: the bud shall yield no meal: if so be it yield, the strangers shall swallow it up.
public_domain_references.brenton: for they sowed blighted [seed], and their destruction shall await them, a sheaf of corn that avails not to make meal; and even if it should produce it, strangers shall devour it.

pob.text: Israel is swallowed up[a]; now they are among the nations like a vessel in which there is no delight.

spob.text: Israel is swallowed up. Now its people are among foreign nations, like a vessel no one wants.

public_domain_references.bsb: Israel is swallowed up! Now they are among the nations like a worthless vessel.
public_domain_references.web: Israel is swallowed up. Now they are among the nations like a worthless thing.
public_domain_references.asv: Israel is swallowed up: now are they among the nations as a vessel wherein none delighteth.
public_domain_references.kjv: Israel is swallowed up: now shall they be among the Gentiles as a vessel wherein [is] no pleasure.
public_domain_references.brenton: Israel is swallowed up: now is he become among the nations as a worthless vessel.

pob.text: For they have gone up to Assyria[a], like a wild donkey wandering alone[b]; Ephraim has hired lovers.

spob.text: For they have gone to Assyria, like a wild donkey wandering by itself. Ephraim has paid for lovers.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: For they have gone up to Assyria like a wild donkey on its own. Ephraim has hired lovers.
public_domain_references.web: For they have gone up to Assyria, like a wild donkey wandering alone. Ephraim has hired lovers for himself.
public_domain_references.asv: For they are gone up to Assyria, [like] a wild ass alone by himself: Ephraim hath hired lovers.
public_domain_references.kjv: For they are gone up to Assyria, a wild ass alone by himself: Ephraim hath hired lovers.
public_domain_references.brenton: For they have gone up to the Assyrians: Ephraim has been strengthened against himself; they loved gifts.

pob.text: Even though they hire among the nations[a], now I will gather them[c][b]; and they will begin to diminish under the burden of the king of princes.

spob.text: Even though they pay to gain allies among the nations,[a] I will now gather them. They will begin to dwindle under the burden of the king who rules over princes.[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: Though they hire allies among the nations, I will now round them up, and they will begin to diminish under the oppression of the king of princes.
public_domain_references.web: But although they sold themselves among the nations, I will now gather them; and they begin to waste away because of the oppression of the king of mighty ones.
public_domain_references.asv: Yea, though they hire among the nations, now will I gather them; and they begin to be diminished by reason of the burden of the king of princes.
public_domain_references.kjv: Yea, though they have hired among the nations, now will I gather them, and they shall sorrow a little for the burden of the king of princes.
public_domain_references.brenton: Therefore shall they be delivered to the nations: now I will receive them, and they shall cease a little to anoint a king and princes.

pob.text: Because Ephraim has multiplied altars for sinning[a], they have become altars for sinning to him.

spob.text: Because Ephraim made more and more altars for sinning,[a] those very altars became altars for sinning for him.

public_domain_references.bsb: Though Ephraim multiplied the altars for sin, they became his altars for sinning.
public_domain_references.web: Because Ephraim has multiplied altars for sinning, they became for him altars for sinning.
public_domain_references.asv: Because Ephraim hath multiplied altars for sinning, altars have been unto him for sinning.
public_domain_references.kjv: Because Ephraim hath made many altars to sin, altars shall be unto him to sin.
public_domain_references.brenton: Because Ephraim has multiplied altars, [his] beloved altars are become sins to him.

pob.text: Though I wrote for him the many things of my law[a], they were regarded as something foreign.

spob.text: Though I wrote many instructions for Israel, Israel treated them as foreign.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Though I wrote for them the great things of My law, they regarded them as something strange.
public_domain_references.web: I wrote for him the many things of my law, but they were regarded as a strange thing.
public_domain_references.asv: I wrote for him the ten thousand things of my law; but they are counted as a strange thing.
public_domain_references.kjv: I have written to him the great things of my law, [but] they were counted as a strange thing.
public_domain_references.brenton: I will write down a multitude [of commands] for him; but his statutes are accounted strange things, [even] the beloved altars.

pob.text: As for the sacrifices of my offerings[a], they sacrifice flesh and eat it, but Yahweh does not accept them. Now he will remember their iniquity and punish their sins[c][b]; they will return to Egypt.

spob.text: As for the sacrificial gifts they offer me, they sacrifice the meat and eat it. But Yahweh does not accept their offerings. Now he will remember their wrongdoing and punish them for their sins. They will return to Egypt.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Though they offer sacrifices as gifts to Me, and though they eat the meat, the LORD does not accept them. Now He will remember their iniquity and punish their sins: They will return to Egypt.
public_domain_references.web: As for the sacrifices of my offerings, they sacrifice meat and eat it, but Yahweh doesn’t accept them. Now he will remember their iniquity, and punish their sins. They will return to Egypt.
public_domain_references.asv: As for the sacrifices of mine offerings, they sacrifice flesh and eat it; but Jehovah accepteth them not: now will he remember their iniquity, and visit their sins; they shall return to Egypt.
public_domain_references.kjv: They sacrifice flesh [for] the sacrifices of mine offerings, and eat [it; but] the LORD accepteth them not; now will he remember their iniquity, and visit their sins: they shall return to Egypt.
public_domain_references.brenton: For if they should offer a sacrifice, and eat flesh, the Lord will not accept them: now will he remember their iniquities, and will take vengeance on their sins: they have returned to Egypt, and they shall eat unclean things among the Assyrians.

pob.text: For Israel has forgotten his Maker and built palaces[a], and Judah has multiplied fortified cities; so I will send fire into his cities, and it will consume her citadels.

spob.text: Israel has forgotten his Maker and built palaces.[a] Judah has built more and more fortified cities. So I will send fire into Judah’s cities, and it will destroy their citadels.

public_domain_references.bsb: Israel has forgotten his Maker and built palaces; Judah has multiplied its fortified cities. But I will send fire upon their cities, and it will consume their citadels.
public_domain_references.web: For Israel has forgotten his Maker and built palaces; and Judah has multiplied fortified cities; but I will send a fire on his cities, and it will devour its fortresses.”
public_domain_references.asv: For Israel hath forgotten his Maker, and builded palaces; and Judah hath multiplied fortified cities: but I will send a fire upon his cities, and it shall devour the castles thereof.
public_domain_references.kjv: For Israel hath forgotten his Maker, and buildeth temples; and Judah hath multiplied fenced cities: but I will send a fire upon his cities, and it shall devour the palaces thereof.
public_domain_references.brenton: And Israel has forgotten him that made him, and they have built fanes, and Juda has multiplied walled cities: but I will send fire on his cities, and it shall devour their foundations.

pob.text: Do not rejoice[a], Israel, with exultation like the peoples, for you have played the prostitute away from your God[b]; you have loved a prostitute’s payment on every threshing floor of grain.

spob.text: Israel, do not celebrate with great joy like the other peoples,[a] because you have acted like a prostitute by turning away from your God. You have loved a prostitute’s payment[b] at every place where grain is threshed.

public_domain_references.bsb: Do not rejoice, O Israel, with exultation like the nations, for you have played the harlot against your God; you have made love for hire on every threshing floor.
public_domain_references.web: Don’t rejoice, Israel, to jubilation like the nations; for you were unfaithful to your God. You love the wages of a prostitute at every grain threshing floor.
public_domain_references.asv: Rejoice not, O Israel, for joy, like the peoples; for thou hast played the harlot, [departing] from thy God; thou hast loved hire upon every grain-floor.
public_domain_references.kjv: Rejoice not, O Israel, for joy, as [other] people: for thou hast gone a whoring from thy God, thou hast loved a reward upon every cornfloor.
public_domain_references.brenton: Rejoice not, O Israel, neither make merry, as [other] nations: for thou hast gone a-whoring from thy God; thou hast loved gifts upon every threshing-floor.

pob.text: Threshing floor and winepress will not feed them[a], and new wine will fail her.

spob.text: The grain from the threshing floor and the wine from the winepress will not feed them. The new wine will fail her—that is, Israel.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: The threshing floor and winepress will not feed them, and the new wine will fail them.
public_domain_references.web: The threshing floor and the wine press won’t feed them, and the new wine will fail her.
public_domain_references.asv: The threshing-floor and the winepress shall not feed them, and the new wine shall fail her.
public_domain_references.kjv: The floor and the winepress shall not feed them, and the new wine shall fail in her.
public_domain_references.brenton: The threshing-floor and wine-press knew them not, and the wine disappointed them.

pob.text: They will not remain in the land of Yahweh[a]; Ephraim will return to Egypt[c][b], and in Assyria they will eat unclean food.

spob.text: They will no longer live in Yahweh’s land. Ephraim will return to Egypt,[a] and in Assyria they will eat food that is unclean under Yahweh’s law.

public_domain_references.bsb: They will not remain in the land of the LORD; Ephraim will return to Egypt and eat unclean food in Assyria.
public_domain_references.web: They won’t dwell in Yahweh’s land; but Ephraim will return to Egypt, and they will eat unclean food in Assyria.
public_domain_references.asv: They shall not dwell in Jehovah’s land; but Ephraim shall return to Egypt, and they shall eat unclean food in Assyria.
public_domain_references.kjv: They shall not dwell in the LORD’s land; but Ephraim shall return to Egypt, and they shall eat unclean [things] in Assyria.
public_domain_references.brenton: They dwelt not in the Lord's land: Ephraim dwelt in Egypt, and they shall eat unclean things among the Assyrians.

pob.text: They will not pour out wine offerings to Yahweh[a], and their sacrifices will not please him. They will be like mourners’ bread to them; all who eat it will become unclean. For their bread will be for themselves alone[b]; it will not enter the house of Yahweh.

spob.text: They will not pour out wine offerings to Yahweh, and he will not accept their sacrifices. Their sacrifices will be like mourners’ bread: everyone who eats it will become ritually unclean. Their bread will be only for feeding themselves; it will not be allowed into Yahweh’s house.

public_domain_references.bsb: They will not pour out wine offerings to the LORD, and their sacrifices will not please Him, but will be to them like the bread of mourners; all who eat will be defiled. For their bread will be for themselves; it will not enter the house of the LORD.
public_domain_references.web: They won’t pour out wine offerings to Yahweh, neither will they be pleasing to him. Their sacrifices will be to them like the bread of mourners; all who eat of it will be polluted; for their bread will be for their appetite. It will not come into Yahweh’s house.
public_domain_references.asv: They shall not pour out wine-[offerings] to Jehovah, neither shall they be pleasing unto him: their sacrifices shall be unto them as the bread of mourners; all that eat thereof shall be polluted; for their bread shall be for their appetite; it shall not come into the house of Jehovah.
public_domain_references.kjv: They shall not offer wine [offerings] to the LORD, neither shall they be pleasing unto him: their sacrifices [shall be] unto them as the bread of mourners; all that eat thereof shall be polluted: for their bread for their soul shall not come into the house of the LORD.
public_domain_references.brenton: They have not offered wine to the Lord, neither have their sacrifices been sweet to him, [but] as the bread of mourning to them; all that eat them shall be defiled; for their bread for their soul shall not enter into the house of the Lord.

pob.text: What will you do on the day of appointed assembly[a], and on the day of the feast of Yahweh?

spob.text: What will you do when the appointed day for the sacred gathering[a] arrives, and when it is time for Yahweh’s feast?

public_domain_references.bsb: What will you do on the appointed day, on the day of the LORD’s feast?
public_domain_references.web: What will you do in the day of solemn assembly, and in the day of the feast of Yahweh?
public_domain_references.asv: What will ye do in the day of solemn assembly, and in the day of the feast of Jehovah?
public_domain_references.kjv: What will ye do in the solemn day, and in the day of the feast of the LORD?
public_domain_references.brenton: What will ye do in the day of the general assembly, and in the day of the feast of the Lord?

pob.text: For behold[a], they have gone away from destruction; Egypt will gather them, Memphis will bury them. Nettles will possess the precious things of their silver; thorns will be in their tents.

spob.text: Look! They have fled from destruction, but Egypt will gather them, and Memphis will bury them. Nettles[a] will take over their precious silver treasures, and thorns will be in their tents.

public_domain_references.bsb: For even if they flee destruction, Egypt will gather them and Memphis will bury them. Their precious silver will be taken over by thistles, and thorns will overrun their tents.
public_domain_references.web: For, behold, when they flee destruction, Egypt will gather them up. Memphis will bury them. Nettles will possess their pleasant things of silver. Thorns will be in their tents.
public_domain_references.asv: For, lo, they are gone away from destruction; [yet] Egypt shall gather them up, Memphis shall bury them; their pleasant things of silver, nettles shall possess them; thorns shall be in their tents.
public_domain_references.kjv: For, lo, they are gone because of destruction: Egypt shall gather them up, Memphis shall bury them: the pleasant [places] for their silver, nettles shall possess them: thorns [shall be] in their tabernacles.
public_domain_references.brenton: Therefore, behold, they go forth from the trouble of Egypt, and Memphis shall receive them, and Machmas shall bury them: [as for] their silver, destruction shall inherit it; thorns [shall be] in their tents.

pob.text: The days of punishment have come[a]; the days of repayment have come; Israel will know it. The prophet is a fool; the man of the spirit is mad[c][b], because of the greatness of your iniquity and your great hostility.

spob.text: The days of punishment are here. The days of repayment are here. Israel will realize this. The prophet is a fool. The person with spiritual inspiration[a] is mad.[b] This is because your wickedness is so great and your hostility so intense.[c]

public_domain_references.bsb: The days of punishment have come; the days of retribution have arrived— let Israel know it. The prophet is called a fool, and the inspired man insane, because of the greatness of your iniquity and hostility.
public_domain_references.web: The days of visitation have come. The days of reckoning have come. Israel will consider the prophet to be a fool, and the man who is inspired to be insane, because of the abundance of your sins, and because your hostility is great.
public_domain_references.asv: The days of visitation are come, the days of recompense are come; Israel shall know it: the prophet is a fool, the man that hath the spirit is mad, for the abundance of thine iniquity, and because the enmity is great.
public_domain_references.kjv: The days of visitation are come, the days of recompence are come; Israel shall know [it:] the prophet [is] a fool, the spiritual man [is] mad, for the multitude of thine iniquity, and the great hatred.
public_domain_references.brenton: The days of vengeance are come, the days of thy recompense are come; and Israel shall be afflicted as the prophet that is mad, as a man deranged: by reason of the multitude of thine iniquities thy madness has abounded.

pob.text: Ephraim’s watchman is with my God[a]; the prophet is a fowler’s snare on all his ways[b], and hostility is in the house of his God.

spob.text: Ephraim’s watchman is with my God.[a] The prophet is a bird-catcher’s trap along all his paths, and there is hostility in the house of his God.

public_domain_references.bsb: The prophet is Ephraim’s watchman, along with my God, yet the snare of the fowler lies on all his paths. Hostility is in the house of his God!
public_domain_references.web: A prophet watches over Ephraim with my God. A fowler’s snare is on all of his paths, and hostility in the house of his God.
public_domain_references.asv: Ephraim [was] a watchman with my God: as for the prophet, a fowler’s snare is in all his ways, [and] enmity in the house of his God.
public_domain_references.kjv: The watchman of Ephraim [was] with my God: [but] the prophet [is] a snare of a fowler in all his ways, [and] hatred in the house of his God.
public_domain_references.brenton: The watchman of Ephraim [was] with God: the prophet is a crooked snare in all his ways: they have established madness in the house of God.

pob.text: They have gone deep into corruption[a], as in the days of Gibeah; he will remember their iniquity[b]; he will punish their sins.

spob.text: They have sunk deep into corruption, just as Israel did in the days of Gibeah.[a] He will remember their wrongdoing and punish them for their sins.

public_domain_references.bsb: They have deeply corrupted themselves as in the days of Gibeah; He will remember their guilt; He will punish their sins.
public_domain_references.web: They have deeply corrupted themselves, as in the days of Gibeah. He will remember their iniquity. He will punish them for their sins.
public_domain_references.asv: They have deeply corrupted themselves, as in the days of Gibeah: he will remember their iniquity, he will visit their sins.
public_domain_references.kjv: They have deeply corrupted [themselves], as in the days of Gibeah: [therefore] he will remember their iniquity, he will visit their sins.
public_domain_references.brenton: They have corrupted themselves according to the days of the hill: he will remember their iniquities, he will take vengeance on their sins.

pob.text: Like grapes in the wilderness I found Israel[a]; like the first-ripe fruit on the fig tree in its first season I saw your fathers. They came to Baal-peor and consecrated themselves to shame[d][c][b], and they became detestable like the thing they loved.

spob.text: I found Israel like grapes in the wilderness. I saw your fathers[a] like the first ripe fig of the season on a fig tree.[b] But they came to Baal-peor and devoted themselves to shame.[c] They became detestable, like the thing they loved.

public_domain_references.bsb: I found Israel like grapes in the wilderness. I saw your fathers as the firstfruits of the fig tree in its first season. But they went to Baal-peor, and consecrated themselves to Shame; so they became as detestable as the thing they loved.
public_domain_references.web: I found Israel like grapes in the wilderness. I saw your fathers as the first ripe in the fig tree at its first season; but they came to Baal Peor, and consecrated themselves to the shameful thing, and became abominable like that which they loved.
public_domain_references.asv: I found Israel like grapes in the wilderness; I saw your fathers as the first-ripe in the fig-tree at its first season: but they came to Baal-peor, and consecrated themselves unto the shameful thing, and became abominable like that which they loved.
public_domain_references.kjv: I found Israel like grapes in the wilderness; I saw your fathers as the firstripe in the fig tree at her first time: [but] they went to Baal-peor, and separated themselves unto [that] shame; and [their] abominations were according as they loved.
public_domain_references.brenton: I found Israel as grapes in the wilderness, and I saw their fathers as an early watchman in a fig-tree: they went in to Beel-phegor, and were shamefully estranged, and the abominable became as the beloved.

pob.text: Ephraim—their glory will fly away like a bird—from birth[a], from the womb[b], and from conception.

spob.text: Ephraim’s glory[a] will fly away like a bird. It will be lost at every stage of having children—from birth, back through the womb, to conception.

public_domain_references.bsb: Ephraim’s glory will fly away like a bird, with no birth, no pregnancy, and no conception.
public_domain_references.web: As for Ephraim, their glory will fly away like a bird. There will be no birth, no one with child, and no conception.
public_domain_references.asv: As for Ephraim, their glory shall fly away like a bird: there shall be no birth, and none with child, and no conception.
public_domain_references.kjv: [As for] Ephraim, their glory shall fly away like a bird, from the birth, and from the womb, and from the conception.
public_domain_references.brenton: Ephraim has flown away as a bird; their glories from the birth, and the travail, and the conception.

pob.text: Even if they raise their children[a], I will bereave them so that not a man remains; for indeed[b], woe to them when I depart from them.

spob.text: Even if they raise their children,[a] I will make them lose those children until not one is left. Yes, woe to them when I depart from them![b]

public_domain_references.bsb: Even if they raise their children, I will bereave them of each one. Yes, woe be to them when I turn away from them!
public_domain_references.web: Though they bring up their children, yet I will bereave them, so that not a man shall be left. Indeed, woe also to them when I depart from them!
public_domain_references.asv: Though they bring up their children, yet will I bereave them, so that not a man shall be left: yea, woe also to them when I depart from them!
public_domain_references.kjv: Though they bring up their children, yet will I bereave them, [that there shall] not [be] a man [left:] yea, woe also to them when I depart from them!
public_domain_references.brenton: For even if they should rear their children, yet shall they be utterly bereaved: wherefore also there is woe to them, [though] my flesh is of them.

pob.text: Ephraim[a], as I have seen, is planted in a pleasant pasture like Tyre[c][b]; but Ephraim must bring out his children to the killer.

spob.text: I have seen Ephraim planted like Tyre in a pleasant pasture.[a] Yet Ephraim must bring his children out to the killer.[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: I have seen Ephraim, like Tyre, planted in a meadow. But Ephraim will bring out his children for slaughter.
public_domain_references.web: I have seen Ephraim, like Tyre, planted in a pleasant place; but Ephraim will bring out his children to the murderer.
public_domain_references.asv: Ephraim, like as I have seen Tyre, is planted in a pleasant place: but Ephraim shall bring out his children to the slayer.
public_domain_references.kjv: Ephraim, as I saw Tyrus, [is] planted in a pleasant place: but Ephraim shall bring forth his children to the murderer.
public_domain_references.brenton: Ephraim, [even] as I saw, gave their children for a prey; yea, Ephraim [was ready] to bring out his children to slaughter.

pob.text: Give them[a], O Yahweh—what will you give? Give them a miscarrying womb and dry breasts.

spob.text: Give them, Yahweh—but what will you give them? Give them wombs that miscarry and breasts that give no milk.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Give them, O LORD— what will You give? Give them wombs that miscarry and breasts that dry up!
public_domain_references.web: Give them—Yahweh what will you give? Give them a miscarrying womb and dry breasts.
public_domain_references.asv: Give them, O Jehovah—what wilt thou give? give them a miscarrying womb and dry breasts.
public_domain_references.kjv: Give them, O LORD: what wilt thou give? give them a miscarrying womb and dry breasts.
public_domain_references.brenton: Give them, O Lord: what wilt thou give them? a miscarrying womb, and dry breasts.

pob.text: All their evil is at Gilgal[a]; indeed, there I hated them because of the evil of their deeds. I will drive them out of my house; I will no longer love them[c][b]. All their princes are rebels.

spob.text: All their evil is at Gilgal.[a] Indeed, it was there that I hated them because of their evil deeds. I will drive them out of my house.[b] I will no longer love them. All their leaders are rebels.[c]

pob.text: Israel is a luxuriant vine that yields fruit for himself[a]. The more his fruit increased, the more he multiplied altars; the better his land became[c][b], the better they made the sacred pillars.

public_domain_references.brenton: Israel is a vine with goodly branches, her fruit is abundant: according to the multitude of her fruits she has multiplied [her] altars; according to the wealth of his land, he has set up pillars.

public_domain_references.brenton: They have divided their hearts; now shall they be utterly destroyed: he shall dig down their altars, their pillars shall mourn.

pob.text: The high places of Aven[a], the sin of Israel, will be destroyed. Thorn and thistle will grow up on their altars, and they will say to the mountains, “Cover us!” and to the hills, “Fall on us!”

public_domain_references.web: The high places also of Aven, the sin of Israel, will be destroyed. The thorn and the thistle will come up on their altars. They will tell the mountains, “Cover us!” and the hills, “Fall on us!”

public_domain_references.brenton: And the altars of On, the sins of Israel, shall be taken away: thorns and thistles shall come up on their altars; and they shall say to the mountains, Cover us; and to the hills, Fall on us.

pob.text: Ephraim was a trained heifer that loved to thresh[a], but I spared her fair neck. I will put Ephraim to the yoke; Judah will plow[c][b]; Jacob will harrow for him.

public_domain_references.brenton: Ephraim is a heifer taught to love victory, but I will come upon the fairest part of her neck: I will mount Ephraim; I will pass over Juda in silence; Jacob shall prevail against him.

public_domain_references.bsb: Sow for yourselves righteousness and reap the fruit of loving devotion; break up your unplowed ground. For it is time to seek the LORD until He comes and sends righteousness upon you like rain.
public_domain_references.web: Sow to yourselves in righteousness, reap according to kindness. Break up your fallow ground, for it is time to seek Yahweh, until he comes and rains righteousness on you.
